title: Greetings & Farewells
description: Learn the standard ways to greet people, ask how they are, and say goodbye in neutral and informal everyday encounters.

title: Politeness & Survival Expressions
description: Master the first interaction formulas needed to be polite, repair communication, and manage simple social exchanges from the first lesson onward.

title: Classroom Language & Communication Repair
description: Handle the mini-language of the classroom: ask what something means, request repetition, and signal that you do or do not understand.

title: Alphabet & Spelling
description: Recognize the German alphabet and spell names, places, and contact details aloud when filling in forms or introducing yourself.

title: Numbers, Telephone Numbers & Email Details
description: Use numbers for age, prices, room numbers, phone numbers, and simple contact information.

lexical_items.pattern: Unit + und + tens: einundzwanzig, zweiunddreißig, vierundfünfzig.

title: Countries, Cities, Languages & Origin
description: Talk about where someone comes from, where they live, and which language they speak.

lexical_items.pattern: Use in for location and aus for origin from countries, cities, and some places.

title: Introductions, Personal Information & Formal vs Informal Address
description: Introduce yourself and others, exchange basic personal details, and distinguish between du and Sie in beginner contexts.

lexical_items.pattern: Use du for informal singular; use Sie for formal singular and plural.

title: Personal Pronouns
description: Use nominative personal pronouns to build very simple statements about yourself and other people.

lexical_items.pattern: ich / du / er / sie / es / wir / ihr / sie

title: The Verb sein in the Present Tense
description: Conjugate sein to say who someone is, where someone is, and basic facts about people or things.

lexical_items.text: sein — ich bin, du bist, er/sie/es ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie/Sie sind

title: Self-Introduction Verbs
description: Use the core beginner verbs for name, origin, residence, and language ability in simple present-tense statements.

lexical_items.translation: to be called / to be named

title: Regular Present-Tense Verb Conjugation
description: Conjugate common regular verbs in the present tense and match endings to the subject pronoun.

lexical_items.pattern: ich -e / du -st / er-sie-es -t / wir -en / ihr -t / sie-Sie -en

title: Stem-Changing Irregular Verbs in the Present
description: Recognize the most frequent vowel-changing verbs and use their du and er/sie/es forms correctly.

title: The Verb haben
description: Use haben for possession and many everyday statements about what people have, need, or carry.

lexical_items.text: haben — ich habe, du hast, er/sie/es hat, wir haben, ihr habt, sie/Sie haben

title: W-Questions
description: Ask for names, places, origins, times, reasons, and things using the core German question words.

lexical_items.pattern: Question word + verb + subject + rest

title: Statements, Yes-No Questions & Verb-Second Word Order
description: Build simple statements and turn them into yes-no questions while keeping the finite verb in the correct position.

lexical_items.pattern: Subject + finite verb + rest
Finite verb + subject + rest
In main clauses, the conjugated verb is the second element.

title: Nouns, Gender & Articles in the Nominative
description: Learn that every German noun has grammatical gender and that the article normally has to be learned together with the noun.

lexical_items.pattern: der + masculine noun / die + feminine noun / das + neuter noun
ein + masculine or neuter noun / eine + feminine noun

title: Plural Forms & Everyday Objects
description: Notice the most common plural patterns and build a first core vocabulary for classroom and daily objects.

lexical_items.pattern: Learn each noun with its plural form because plural endings vary.
Common beginner plural endings include -e, -er, -n/-en, -s, and zero ending.

title: Negation with nicht and kein
description: Negate whole statements, adjectives, and nouns with the two basic beginner negation patterns.

lexical_items.pattern: Use nicht to negate verbs, adjectives, adverbs, or a whole clause.
Use kein instead of an indefinite article to negate a noun.

title: Family Words & Possessive Articles
description: Talk about family members and say whose person or thing something is using basic possessive forms.

lexical_items.pattern: Use mein with masculine/neuter nouns and meine with feminine/plural nouns in the nominative.
Use dein with masculine/neuter nouns and deine with feminine/plural nouns in the nominative.
Use Ihr / Ihre for formal 'your'.

title: Professions, Study & Basic Workplaces
description: Say what someone does, where someone works or studies, and understand a small everyday set of job nouns.

title: Days, Parts of the Day, Months, Seasons & Dates
description: Name the calendar words needed for plans, routines, birthdays, travel, and the first simple date expressions.

lexical_items.pattern: Use ordinal numbers for dates: am ersten Mai, am dritten Juli.
Use am with days, dates, and parts of the day.
Use im with months and seasons.

title: Telling Time & Making Appointments
description: Tell the time, ask when something happens, and make or confirm simple appointments.

lexical_items.translation: Do you have time on Monday?

lexical_items.pattern: Use um with clock times.
Use von ... bis to express a start and end time span.

title: Daily Routine Verbs
description: Describe a simple day using high-frequency routine verbs in the present tense.

lexical_items.text: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
lexical_items.translation: I get up at seven o'clock.

title: Modal Verbs müssen and wollen
description: Express basic necessity and intention, especially for everyday obligations and simple plans.

lexical_items.translation: We want to go to the cinema.

lexical_items.pattern: Subject + müssen/wollen + rest + infinitive

title: Hobbies, Free Time & the Modal Verb können
description: Talk about what you can do and what you like doing in your free time.

lexical_items.pattern: Subject + modal verb + rest + infinitive

title: Food, Drinks, Preferences & mögen / möchten
description: Name common food and drink categories and express likes, dislikes, and simple wants in cafés or at home.

title: Ordering Food, Paying & Restaurant Expressions
description: Use the fixed expressions needed to order, ask for the bill, and manage a very short café or restaurant exchange.

title: Shopping, Prices, Colors & Basic Adjectives
description: Ask about prices, describe simple objects, and use colors and easy adjectives to choose or evaluate things.

lexical_items.pattern: Use sein + adjective: Das ist schön. / Die Wohnung ist groß.

title: Home, Rooms & Furniture
description: Describe where you live and name the most important rooms and furniture items in simple housing conversations.

title: The Accusative Case & Common Accusative Verbs
description: Use the accusative for direct objects with the most frequent beginner verbs and article forms.

lexical_items.pattern: den + masculine noun / die + feminine noun / das + neuter noun
einen + masculine noun / eine + feminine noun / ein + neuter noun

title: Places in Town, Orientation & Transportation
description: Name common places and means of transport, and understand the core vocabulary for navigating a city.

title: Asking for Directions & Simple Route Phrases
description: Ask where a place is and understand very simple route instructions in shops, stations, and cities.

lexical_items.translation: Excuse me, where is the station?

lexical_items.pattern: Use es gibt to say that something exists or is available.

title: Separable Verbs & the Sentence Bracket
description: Understand that some common verbs split in the present tense and send their prefix to the end of the clause.

lexical_items.pattern: In main clauses the prefix moves to the end: aufstehen → Ich stehe um sieben auf.

title: Body Parts, Symptoms & Basic Doctor Phrases
description: Name the most useful body parts and say in a very simple way what hurts or what is wrong.

lexical_items.translation: I have to go to the doctor.

title: Invitations, Plans & Accepting or Refusing
description: Make simple social plans, invite someone, and answer with easy acceptance or refusal formulas.

lexical_items.translation: Shall we go to the café?

lexical_items.text: Tut mir leid, ich kann nicht.
